Main.sentence: Illinois's first congressional district is a ___E:congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_district)___ in the U.S. state of ___E:Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois)___ .

Based in ___E:Cook County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_County,_Illinois)___ , the district includes much of the South Side of ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ and continues southwest to ___E:Joliet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joliet,_Illinois)___ .

From 2003 to early 2013 it extended into the city's ___E:southwest suburbs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_metropolitan_area)___ until reaching the border of ___E:Will County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_County,_Illinois)___ , and covered 97.84 square miles (253.4 km 2 ), making it one of the ___E:40 smallest districts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_congressional_districts_by_area)___ in the U.S. (although there are four smaller districts in Illinois).
The district had a population that was 65% African American, the highest percentage of any congressional district in the nation, but with redistricting that percentage has now declined to 52%.

It includes the home of former ___E:President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , who ran unsuccessfully for the seat in the ___E:2000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Illinois%27s_1st_congressional_district_election)___ primary.
The 1st is a ___E:majority-minority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majority-minority)___ district, and has been since at least the 1920s.

In 1929, it became the first district in the 20th century to send an ___E:African American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American)___ to Congress when ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ ___E:Oscar Stanton De Priest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Stanton_De_Priest)___ was elected to represent the district.
The 1st has been represented by an African American Member of Congress ever since, the longest ongoing stretch of black representation for any seat in the House of Representatives.

It has been held by a ___E:Democrat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ since 1935 when ___E:Arthur Mitchell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_W._Mitchell)___ , the first African American Democrat elected to Congress, took the seat as part of the ___E:New Deal Coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal_Coalition)___ .
In 1949, district representative ___E:William Dawson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_L._Dawson_(politician))___ became the first African American to chair a congressional committee.

The district is currently represented by ___E:Jonathan Jackson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Jackson_(Illinois_politician))___ who was elected to succeed longtime incumbent ___E:Bobby Rush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Rush)___ in 2022.

As of the 2020 redistricting, the district will still be centered primarily around the ___E:Chicago's South Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago%27s_South_Side)___ , now with a greater portion of ___E:Will U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_County,_Illinois)___ County, and a corner of northern ___E:Kankakee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kankakee_County,_Illinois)___ County.

The 1st district takes in the ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago,_Illinois)___ neighborhoods of ___E:Oakland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Burnham Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnham_Park,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Auburn Gresham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_Gresham,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Washington Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Heights,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Greater Grand Crossing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Grand_Crossing,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Chatham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatham,_Chicago)___ , and ___E:Burnside U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnside,_Chicago)___ ; most of ___E:Ashburn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Roseland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseland,_Chicago)___ , and ___E:Calumet Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_Heights,_Chicago)___ ; the west portion of ___E:Kenwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenwood,_Chicago)___ and ___E:Woodlawn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodlawn,_Chicago)___ ; and parts of ___E:South Deering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Deering,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Near South Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near_South_Side,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Chicago Lawn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Lawn,_Chicago)___ , ___E:South Shore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Shore,_Chicago)___ , ___E:South Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Chicago,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Washington Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Park_(community_area),_Chicago)___ , ___E:Morgan Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Park,_Chicago)___ , and ___E:Mt. Outside of the Chicago city limits, the district takes in the ___E:Cook U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_County,_Illinois)___ County communities of ___E:Midlothian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midlothian,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Posen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posen,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Robbins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbins,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Calumet Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_Park,_Illinois)___ , and ___E:Palos Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palos_Park,_Illinois)___ ; most of ___E:Blue Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Island,_Illinois)___ ; the south portion of ___E:Lemont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemont,_Illinois)___ ; the eastern portion of ___E:Alsip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alsip,_Illinois)___ ; the northeastern portion of ___E:Evergreen Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evergreen_Park,_Illinois)___ ; the western portion of ___E:Markham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markham,_Illinois)___ ; the southeastern portion of ___E:Tinley Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tinley_Park,_Illinois)___ ; and parts of ___E:Oak Forest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Forest,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Orland Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orland_Park,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Crestwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crestwood,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Beverly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Riverdale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Dixmoor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixmoor,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Harvey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Country Club Hills U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Club_Hills,_Illinois)___ , and ___E:Matteson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matteson,_Illinois)___ .

The 1st district takes in the municipalities of ___E:Manteno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manteno,_Illinois)___ , northern ___E:Bourbannais U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbonnais,_Illinois)___ , and part of ___E:Bradley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley,_Illinois)___ .

The departure of the ___E:steel industry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_modern_steel_industry)___ , along with other manufacturing jobs from the South Side in recent decades, has created economic difficulties which the area is still trying to overcome.
The district's median household income as of 2000, $37,222, trailed the national average by 11.4%.
The unemployment rate (7.6%) was more than double the national rate, and nearly 20% of district residents were living in poverty.

These problems are more pronounced within the Chicago portion of the district – 14 of the district's 18 suburbs had median household incomes over $40,000 as of 1999, with the six most affluent grouped in the southwest corner of the district.

But black middle-class Chicago neighborhoods, such as Avalon Park and Chatham, have remained more stable, along with the more upscale Hyde Park-Kenwood area. ___E:Health care U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care_in_the_United_States)___ and ___E:higher education U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universities_in_the_United_States)___ now constitute major economic sectors in the region.

Hospitals in the district include ___E:Oak Forest Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Forest_Hospital_of_Cook_County)___ in Oak Forest and ___E:Provident Hospital of Cook County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provident_Hospital_(Chicago))___ in Grand Boulevard, both part of the ___E:Cook County Bureau of Health Services U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cook_County_Bureau_of_Health_Services&action=edit&redlink=1)___ ; as well as the ___E:University of Chicago Hospitals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Hospitals)___ in Hyde Park, ___E:Little Company of Mary Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Company_of_Mary_Hospital_(Evergreen_Park))___ in Evergreen Park, ___E:Holy Cross Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Cross_Hospital_(Chicago))___ in Chicago Lawn, ___E:St. Francis Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSM_Health_Care)___ in Blue Island, ___E:Jackson Park Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jackson_Park_Hospital&action=edit&redlink=1)___ in South Shore and ___E:St. Bernard Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Bernard_Hospital&action=edit&redlink=1)___ in Englewood.

Local educational institutions include the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ in Hyde Park, ___E:Illinois Institute of Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Institute_of_Technology)___ (IIT) in Douglas, ___E:Trinity Christian College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_Christian_College)___ in Palos Heights and ___E:Kennedy-King College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy-King_College)___ , a ___E:Chicago city college U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Colleges_of_Chicago)___ , in Englewood, and ___E:Chicago State University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_State_University)___ in Roseland is located directly outside the district at its southern edge; in addition, there are five seminaries in Hyde Park: ___E:Catholic Theological Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Theological_Union)___ , ___E:Chicago Theological Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Theological_Seminary)___ , ___E:Lutheran School of Theology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheran_School_of_Theology_at_Chicago)___ , ___E:McCormick Theological Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCormick_Theological_Seminary)___ and ___E:Meadville Lombard Theological School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meadville_Lombard_Theological_School)___ .

___E:Rate Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rate_Field)___ , home of the ___E:Chicago White Sox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox)___ , is less than 1,000 feet (300 m) west of the district's northwestern border.

Other area cultural and entertainment attractions include the ___E:DuSable Museum of African American History U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DuSable_Museum)___ in Chicago's ___E:Washington Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Park_(Chicago_park))___ , and ___E:First Midwest Bank Amphitheatre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Midwest_Bank_Amphitheatre)___ in Tinley Park; several square miles of ___E:Cook County Forest Preserves U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_County_Forest_Preserves)___ can be found on three sides of Oak Forest, and Oak Forest's Chicago Gaelic Park ___E: U:(http://www.chicagogaelicpark.org/)___ is home to Irish Fest, held annually on Memorial Day weekend.

Business and industrial presences in the district include Panduit Corporation ___E: U:(http://www.panduit.com/)___ , an electrical manufacturer in Tinley Park; Parco Foods ___E: U:(http://www.parcofoods.com/)___ , a cookie manufacturer in Blue Island; and Midwest Suburban Publishing, publisher of the SouthtownStar , in Tinley Park.

In addition to Washington Park and those sites associated with the University of Chicago and IIT, district locations on the ___E:National Register of Historic Places U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places)___ include:
Democrats routinely dominate politics in the district, with the main focus of competition being the party ___E:primary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_primary)___ .

Only twice since 1966 has a Republican candidate for Congress received over 20% of the vote,  and the Democratic nominee has topped 80% in every ___E:presidential race U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election)___ during that time. The district's expansion into the suburbs in the 1990s has incorporated a population that has voted Republican more often; Republican support has passed the 10% mark, and ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ received 17% of the vote here in ___E:2004 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election)___ .
His was the best showing by a Republican presidential candidate in the district in over 40 years.

The district has since the early 1970s elected representatives who dissented from the city's Democratic establishment. ___E:William L. Dawson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_L._Dawson_(politician))___ , U.S.
Representative from 1943 to 1970, maintained the district's loyalty to Mayor ___E:Richard J. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_J._Daley)___ .

His successor ___E:Ralph Metcalfe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Metcalfe)___ initially continued that stance but publicly broke with Daley over an incident of police brutality in 1972, establishing a rift that persists.

When Metcalfe died less than one month before the election in ___E:1978 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_elections,_1978)___ , Democratic party officials named loyalist ___E:Bennett M. Stewart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bennett_M._Stewart)___ to take his place on the ballot, and Republicans replaced their candidate with ___E:A.A. "Sammy" Rayner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sammy_Rayner&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , a former Democratic alderman.
Despite the campaign support of Jackson for Rayner, Stewart won the election, although Rayner did get over 40% of the vote.
Stewart served only one term and lost the 1980 Democratic primary to reform candidate ___E:Harold Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Washington)___ .

He left Congress in 1983 upon being elected mayor, after winning a contentious three-way primary with 37% of the vote. His successor in Congress was union organizer ___E:Charles Hayes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Hayes_(politician))___ .

Hayes lost the ___E:1992 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_elections,_1992)___ primary to ___E:Bobby Rush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Rush)___ by a 42–39% margin following the ___E:House banking scandal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_banking_scandal)___ , in which it was revealed that Hayes had 716 overdrafts on his congressional checking account.
Rush had previously lost the 1988 and 1990 primaries to Hayes.

Rush was a co-founder of the Illinois ___E:Black Panthers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Panther_Party)___ in 1968, establishing a program for free breakfasts for poor children and a clinic for ___E:sickle cell anemia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sickle_cell_anemia)___ screenings.

He served as a Chicago alderman from 1983 until his election to Congress in 1993, and he was an ally of Mayor Washington in the ___E:Council Wars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_Wars)___ of the 1980s.

While in Congress, Rush consistently voted with the Democratic position over 90% of the time. When he did break from the party, he usually took positions more liberal than other Democrats, rather than taking positions held by Republicans.
Rush ran against incumbent ___E:Richard M. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_M._Daley)___ in the 1999 election for Mayor of Chicago.

Despite the support of fellow congressmen ___E:Jesse Jackson Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Jackson_Jr.)___ and ___E:Danny Davis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_K._Davis)___ , he was backed by only three out of 50 aldermen and lost the election by a margin of 72–28%.
He had a 55–45% advantage among black voters.

In the ___E:2000 congressional primary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois%27s_1st_congressional_district_election,_2000)___ Rush emerged with a 61–30% win over challenger ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ resulting in Obama's only electoral defeat.

In Congress, Rush focused on ___E:urban revitalization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_renewal)___ issues, and he was a staunch supporter of ___E:gun control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_politics_in_the_United_States)___ efforts before his adult son Huey (named for Black Panther leader ___E:Huey Newton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huey_Newton)___ ) was killed in a 1999 ___E:mugging U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mugging_(robbery))___ .
Following his son's murder, Rush remained a strong supporter of gun control.

During his congressional tenure, Rush generally received perfect ratings of 100 from labor groups including the ___E:AFL-CIO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFL-CIO)___ and ___E:AFSCME U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Federation_of_State,_County_and_Municipal_Employees)___ , and occasionally also from ___E:Americans for Democratic Action U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans_for_Democratic_Action)___ , the ___E:ACLU U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_Liberties_Union)___ and the ___E:National Abortion Rights Action League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Abortion_Rights_Action_League)___ .
His lifetime rating from the ___E:American Conservative Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Conservative_Union)___ is 3.93 on a 0 to 100 scale.

The district was adjacent to the ___E:2nd district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois%27s_2nd_congressional_district)___ to the east and south, the ___E:7th district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois%27s_7th_congressional_district)___ to the north, and the ___E:3rd U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois%27s_3rd_congressional_district)___ and ___E:13th districts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois%27s_13th_congressional_district)___ to the west, and also bordered the ___E:11th district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois%27s_11th_congressional_district)___ at its southwest corner.
The district's northeast border followed ___E:Lake Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan)___ 's shoreline for almost a mile.

The district was created following the ___E:1830 U.S. census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1830_United_States_census)___ and came into existence in 1833, five months before Chicago was organized as a town; the state was previously represented in ___E:the U.S. House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ with representative elected on an ___E:at-large U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois%27s_At-large_congressional_district)___ basis.

The district included ___E:Southwestern Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Egypt_(region))___ until 1853.   It included the state's ___E:northern edge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Illinois)___ until 1863.  Since that time, the district has included all or part of Cook County; since 1883 the population of the district has been primarily residing on ___E:Chicago's South Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago%27s_South_Side)___ .
Historical populations reflected waves of immigration into the area: previous majority populations were ethnic Irish, German, and east European.
Beginning in the mid-19th century, the Irish were the first to establish their physical and political control of the area within the city's South Side.

The current 1st district has a ___E:minority-majority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minority-majority)___ population: 51.3% of the residents are ___E:African-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census))___ .

It has been represented in Congress by African Americans since 1929. Tens of thousands of African Americans moved to Chicago from the rural South in the ___E:Great Migration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Migration_(African_American))___ .
They were confined by discrimination to the South Side of Chicago and gradually replaced ethnic whites who moved out to suburbs.
At one point during the 1980s, more than 90% of the district's residents were black.

While successive redistrictings have given the district a larger percentage of white voters, it is still one of the most reliably Democratic districts in the country; with a ___E:Cook Partisan Voting Index U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_Partisan_Voting_Index)___ of D+28, it is the fourth most Democratic district of the eight that divide Chicago.
The district has not sent a ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ to the U.S.
House of Representatives since ___E:1935 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_elections,_1934)___ .

After the ___E:civil rights movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights_movement)___ gained support from national Democratic Party for major legislation to restore constitutional rights, including the franchise in the South, most African Americans shifted to support the Democratic Party.

Democratic congressional candidates routinely receive over 80% of the vote here. The Democratic trend runs right through to the national level; since the 1950s, Democratic presidential candidates have usually carry the district with well over 70 percent of the vote, and have done no worse than 64 percent/
In 2011, following the ___E:2010 census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census)___ , the state legislature redistricted.
It expanded the district to cover parts of ___E:Cook U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook_County,_Illinois)___ and ___E:Will U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_County,_Illinois)___ Counties.

The representative for these districts were elected in the 2012 primary and general elections, and the boundaries became effective on January 3, 2013.

In the twentieth century after the Great Migration from the South and concentration of blacks on the South Side due to de facto residential segregation, the district became the nation's first with a black-majority population.
Since the 1920s, it has included the central area of Chicago's South Side African-American community.

Over 85% of the district's residents were black during the period from the 1950s through the 1980s, but redistricting since that time – which redrew the district lines with the goal of maintaining three Chicago districts with black populations exceeding 60% – has reduced the percentage of black residents in the district to 70% in the 1990s.
The current figure is 65%.

Outward migration has caused the South Side's population to decrease over the years, and the district was expanded geographically to the southwest to gain residents, particularly as the state's congressional delegation has been reduced in numbers due to population changes and reapportionment.
The district, which covered only nine square miles in the 1950s, is now more than ten times that size. Nearly half its current area was added for the 2000s.

The district's population dropped by 27% in the 1950s,  and by 20% in both the 1970s and 1980s, due to outward migration for suburbanization and because of people leaving the area due to loss of jobs.   In redistricting after the ___E:1990 U.S. census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_United_States_census)___ , the district was extended into the suburbs for the first time in 90 years.
Chicago is home to 70% of the district's residents (down from 90% in the 1990s),  although roughly 60% of the district's area is outside the city border.

The district's white population (almost 30% of its residents) is concentrated in the suburban areas and in a few Chicago neighborhoods such as Hyde Park.  The district's largest white ethnic groups are ___E:Irish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_American)___ (7.1%), ___E:German U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_American)___ (6.2%), ___E:Polish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_American)___ (4.5%) and ___E:Italian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_American)___ (3.2%),  mirroring the demographics of the neighboring third and thirteenth congressional districts.
